pattern:
Chunk 1 covers positions 0, 5, ..., 65 of the 66 runs marked wrong=true in canonical/mini-swe-agent-openai-gpt-5-6, 14 runs in all. Only 2 are real model misses; the other 12 are infrastructure.

Infrastructure (12 runs):
- **9 provider stalls in the MPO campaign (2026-09-18/19):** CLOSURE-23-MPO-001 x4, LANG-1-MPO-001 x3, LANG-34-MPO-001 x2. Each trajectory ends on a tool output after 0-28 s of activity and 0-4 API calls, with an empty exit_status and then a 300 s timeout. In 4 of the 9 the gold body had already been displayed (all 3 LANG-1 runs, and LANG-34 run-008). In 3 CLOSURE-23 runs the agent had reached the consumer call site that names getChildAtPosition and, in run-018, was following it.
- **1 pre-launch harness rejection:** CHART-1-L10-STRICT-001. Its placeholder stack trace says 'no gold method appears', which tripped the /gold/i isolation gate.
- **1 legacy protocol mismatch:** Chart-1 run-002. The prompt asked for a plain-text answer, but mini-swe-agent requires a tool call every turn and no submit tool was exposed, so the run ended in RepeatedFormatError. The agent had already re-grepped the exact fault line.
- **1 rejected correct answer:** MOCKITO-28-CC-001 run-002. method_catalog.json held 0 methods, so all 12 submits returned class_not_found even though the gold was at rank 1.

None of these 12 should count as model errors.

The 2 real misses (CLOSURE-131-OWN-001, gold rank 4; GSON-1-DISC-001, gold rank 6) share one mechanism. In both, the agent:
- displayed the full gold body;
- ran the test and saw the failure values;
- named the gold's actual mechanism in its own evidence chain ('table marks it PART_CHAR whereas TokenStream rejects ignorables'; 'toMoreSpecificType converts the ParameterizedType to raw Box.class').

It then ranked a correct neighbour on the same causal path above the gold. That neighbour was a declared decoy: the decision-site reader of the shared table (isSimpleNameChars) or the selection method whose lookup order shows the symptom (getMatchingHandler). The gold was the upstream writer or specializer that sets the wrong value. These are attribution errors, not search failures: the model blames the method where the wrong value is used or becomes visible, not the one that produces it. In GSON this was reinforced by a decoy that looks symptom-matching locally, plus an ignored TODO above the gold.
